headline: Daily market snapshot 2026-07-21
summary: Premarket snapshot Jul 21 2026: S&P 500 futures +0.5% and Nasdaq-100 futures +1.3% as chip stocks rebounded. Prior session (Jul 20) closes: SPX 7443.28 -0.19%, IXIC 25508.07 -0.05%, DJI 51839.26 -0.59%. BTC near $65,500 two-week high, ETH ~$1,907; Brent ~$88.58, gold ~$4,030; DXY 100.92; 10Y yield 4.59%.

headline: Nasdaq leads Dow, S&P 500 futures higher as chip stocks revive on July 21
summary: US stock futures rose Tuesday as investors braced for a busy earnings week, with Nasdaq-100 futures jumping 1.3% as semiconductor names led the rebound. SPY rose 0.56% to $746.28 and QQQ advanced 1.38% to $705.68 in premarket. Easing oil prices and chip-sector recovery offset ongoing Iran-Hormuz tensions.

headline: General Motors Q2 2026 beats estimates with EPS $3.20; raises full-year EBIT guidance
summary: General Motors reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.20 on revenue of $47 billion, beating consensus of $3.13 EPS. The automaker raised its full-year adjusted EBIT outlook to $13.5B–$15.5B and EPS guidance to $11.50–$13.50. Gross tariff exposure was revised down to $2.5B–$3.5B with ~$500M in expected Section 232 tariff refunds following a Supreme Court ruling.
key_facts: Q2 adj EPS $3.20 vs $3.13 est (+26% YoY)

headline: Halliburton reports Q2 2026 earnings July 21; consensus EPS $0.54, revenue $5.5B
summary: Halliburton (HAL) released Q2 2026 results before market open on July 21 with a conference call at 9am ET. Analyst consensus was EPS of $0.54 (down ~1.8% YoY) and revenue of ~$5.5 billion (down ~0.2% YoY), reflecting softer North American drilling activity amid lower oil prices earlier in the year.

headline: 3M Q2 2026 results due July 21; consensus EPS $2.27, revenue $6.38B; strong AI demand cited
summary: 3M Company (MMM) released second-quarter 2026 results before market open on July 21. The consensus estimate called for EPS of $2.27 (+5.1% YoY) and revenue of $6.38 billion (+3.6% YoY), driven by AI-related demand in the Safety and Industrial segment. 3M beat in each of the prior four quarters with an average positive surprise of 4.6%.
key_facts: Beat in 4 of prior 4 quarters; 4.6% avg surprise
Safety & Industrial segment benefits from AI demand

headline: AMC Entertainment Q2 2026: record $1.60B revenue and $321M EBITDA, highest in 106-year history
summary: AMC Entertainment reported Q2 2026 revenues of $1.597 billion (+14.2% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $321.4 million (+70% YoY, margin 20.1%), both the highest in the company's 106-year history. Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.14 (surprise profit), free cash flow reached $190.1 million, and attendance grew 13.5% to 71.3 million patrons. Premium screens drove the outperformance.

headline: AMC Entertainment surges 17.7% premarket after record Q2 results
summary: AMC Entertainment Holdings (AMC) soared 17.7% in premarket trading on July 21 after posting record Q2 2026 revenues of $1.60B and adjusted EBITDA of $321.4M—both 106-year company highs—along with a surprise adjusted net profit of $0.14 per diluted share.

headline: Nvidia discloses 9.3% passive stake in neocloud firm Nebius Group via SEC filing
summary: Nvidia disclosed an SEC filing revealing a 9.3% passive stake in Nebius Group (NBIS), comprising ~1.19 million Class A shares plus a warrant for 21.065 million additional shares obtained via a $2 billion investment completed in March 2026. Nvidia is prohibited from exercising the warrant or selling shares before September 11. NBIS rose ~6.5% in premarket trading on the disclosure.
key_facts: Nvidia holds 9.3% passive stake in Nebius (22.26M shares total)
Stake derives from $2B investment completed March 2026
Cannot sell or exercise before September 11

headline: Freedom Capital upgrades Nebius to Buy with $200 price target after Nvidia stake disclosure
summary: Freedom Capital upgraded Nebius Group (NBIS) to Buy and set a $200 price target following Nvidia's disclosure of a 9.3% passive stake. Shares were at $195.30 in premarket (+6.94%). The analyst cited Nvidia's strategic partnership, strong AI cloud demand, and IREN's rival $4B ARR raise as validating the neocloud sector.
key_facts: Catalyst: Nvidia 9.3% stake + AI cloud demand

headline: Nebius Group jumps 6.94% to $195.30 premarket on Nvidia stake and Buy upgrade
summary: Nebius Group (NBIS) shares jumped 6.94% to $195.30 in premarket trading on July 21 after Nvidia disclosed a 9.3% passive stake via SEC filing (22.26M total shares including a warrant) and Freedom Capital upgraded to Buy with a $200 price target. Analysts called the disclosure the 'Nvidia Effect' for AI cloud infrastructure names.

headline: IREN signs $2.8B AI cloud contracts with Perplexity and Figure AI; raises 2026 ARR target above $4B
summary: IREN Ltd raised its year-end AI cloud annualized run-rate revenue target from $3.7B to over $4B following new multi-year customer contracts totaling $2.8B. Key customers include Microsoft, Nvidia, Perplexity, and Figure AI. Approximately 85% of IREN's revenue is now under contract with a ~4-year weighted average term. Capacity expansion plan targets 1.2 GW by 2027, up from 480 MW in 2026. Cash stood at $7.6B as of June 30.
key_facts: Customers include Microsoft, Nvidia, Perplexity, Figure AI

headline: IREN surges ~20% to $40.20 on $2.8B AI contract haul; bulls target $48
summary: IREN Ltd shares surged approximately 20% to $40.20 (intraday high $41.10) following its $2.8B multi-year AI cloud contract announcement with Perplexity, Figure AI, Microsoft, and Nvidia and its raised ARR target above $4B. Analysts targeting $48 per share based on the improved revenue visibility.

headline: Archer Aviation and Anduril unveil Thunder autonomous VTOL; ACHR surges 20%
summary: Archer Aviation (ACHR) and Anduril Industries jointly unveiled the Thunder, a Group 5 autonomous attack rotorcraft designed to multiply the combat power of crewed helicopters using a series hybrid-electric dual-tiltrotor powertrain. A civilian version (Halo) is also planned. First flight targets 2027; first commercial launch partners to be announced this week. ACHR surged 19.59% to $5.31 on July 20.
key_facts: Commercial launch partners announcement expected this week

headline: Archer Aviation continues Thunder rally on July 21; $6 resistance in focus
summary: Archer Aviation (ACHR) continued to build on Monday's 19.59% surge to $5.31 as the Thunder autonomous VTOL launch gained further investor attention on Tuesday. The next key technical resistance is $6 per share. Archer plans to announce commercial launch partners for the Halo civilian VTOL variant during the week of July 21.
key_facts: Halo commercial launch partners announcement imminent

headline: Iran strikes tanker in Hormuz; US completes fresh overnight strikes; mediators propose 10-day ceasefire
summary: Iran attacked a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz early Tuesday while the US completed a fresh round of airstrikes against Iran overnight—the 10th consecutive day of US military action. Regional mediators presented Washington and Tehran with a proposal for a 10-day ceasefire. However, President Trump said the US would retaliate for American troop deaths; large divisions remain between the two sides.
key_facts: Iran struck tanker in Strait of Hormuz Jul 21
US completed 10th consecutive day of airstrikes vs Iran
Large divisions remain between US and Iran
Trump: US will retaliate for troop deaths

headline: Iran-backed Houthis declare maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia, threatening Red Sea oil routes
summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels declared an immediate maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia after Saudi forces bombed Sanaa International Airport. Saudi Arabia had rerouted ~70% of crude exports (~7M bbl/day) through the Red Sea's Yanbu port after Hormuz disruptions began. The Bab el-Mandeb strait handles ~12% of global trade, 25% of container traffic, and 5% of global oil supply. Saudi Arabia rejected the threat and warned of escalation.
key_facts: Houthi maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia effective immediately
Retaliation for Saudi bombing of Sanaa Airport
Saudi Arabia rerouted ~7M bbl/day through Red Sea after Hormuz closure
Bab el-Mandeb: 12% global trade, 25% containers, 5% oil supply
Saudi Arabia rejected threat, warned of escalation
Rystad Energy warned of potential supply shock

headline: Houthi Saudi blockade opens dual-route energy risk alongside Hormuz crisis
summary: The Houthi maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia, combined with the ongoing Strait of Hormuz disruption, creates an unprecedented dual-route energy supply shock. With Saudi Arabia already rerouting ~7M bbl/day through the Red Sea's Yanbu port, a disruption there would close the largest bypass to the Hormuz blockade. Energy analysts say this scenario is without modern precedent and could drive oil significantly higher.
key_facts: Combined Hormuz + Red Sea = dual supply shock scenario
Bab el-Mandeb carries 12% global trade, 5% oil
Saudi Arabia rerouted ~7M bbl/day to Red Sea to bypass Hormuz
Rystad Energy warns of significant oil price rebound risk
Unprecedented dual-route threat in modern energy markets

headline: Alibaba unveils Qwen3.8 Max LLM claiming #2 rank globally; BABA +4% premarket
summary: Alibaba unveiled a preview of its Qwen3.8 Max large language model, claiming the second-most powerful LLM ranking globally behind Anthropic's Fable 5. Developers gain access via the Token Plan and Qoder/QoderWork platforms ahead of a full open-weight release on July 27. BABA shares rose ~4% in premarket, extending a ~25% rally from late June as Qwen models also won regulatory approval to power Apple Intelligence in China.
key_facts: Qwen3.8 Max claims #2 rank globally (behind Anthropic Fable 5)
Preview via Token Plan and Qoder platforms
BABA at ~$120.80 Jul 20 close; +25% since late June
Qwen models approved to power Apple Intelligence in China

headline: Asian equities rebound 2.2% as chip stocks recover; Nikkei +2.7%, KOSPI +4%, China tech +7%
summary: Asian equities staged a forceful rebound on Tuesday after three days of losses, with the MSCI Asia Pacific Index rising 2.2%. Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 2.7% after entering correction territory last week. South Korea's KOSPI and Taiwan's Taiex both gained ~4%, while mainland China's tech sector surged ~7%. Brent crude eased to ~$88.58 on ceasefire mediation reports, helping cool the inflation scare.
key_facts: Brent fell 0.7% to ~$88.58 on ceasefire mediation

headline: Nikkei 225 gains 2.7% in chip-led rebound after entering correction territory last week
summary: Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 2.7% on Tuesday as AI semiconductor stocks rebounded following last week's correction driven by AI valuation concerns and Iran-energy inflation fears. Renewed demand for Japanese chipmaker and equipment stocks drove the move, with Brent crude easing slightly on ceasefire mediation reports.
key_facts: AI semiconductor stocks led the rebound

headline: South Korea KOSPI and Taiwan Taiex both gain ~4% on semiconductor complex recovery
summary: South Korea's KOSPI and Taiwan's Taiex both gained approximately 4% on Tuesday as investors returned to the semiconductor complex after three consecutive sessions of losses. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix led the Korean recovery, while TSMC rebounded in Taiwan on renewed AI demand confidence.
key_facts: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix led Korean rebound
TSMC bounced on AI demand narrative renewal

headline: China mainland tech sector surges ~7% on AI stock rebound and Alibaba LLM news
summary: Mainland China's technology sector surged approximately 7% on Tuesday, outpacing a flattish broader Shanghai Composite (Jul 20 close 3,796.3 +0.85%). China AI stocks benefited from the global semiconductor rebound and the announcement of Alibaba's Qwen3.8 Max LLM, claimed to rank #2 globally. Nasdaq 100 futures rising 1% also supported the move.
key_facts: Alibaba Qwen3.8 Max LLM claim (#2 globally) a catalyst

headline: Brent crude slips 0.7% to ~$88.58/bbl on ceasefire hopes but Iran tanker attack limits drop
summary: Brent crude fell 0.7% to approximately $88.58 per barrel in early Tuesday trading as mediators proposed a 10-day US-Iran ceasefire, cooling some geopolitical premium. However, an overnight Iranian tanker strike in the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthi maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia prevented a steeper decline. Brent had rallied sharply since the conflict resumed around July 9.
key_facts: Houthi Saudi embargo added upward pressure

headline: WTI crude oil trades in $81-$83 range on July 21 amid geopolitical uncertainty
summary: WTI crude oil futures traded in the $81.41–$83.22 per barrel range on July 21, up significantly from ~$68/bbl before the Iran-Hormuz conflict resumed in July. The market was balancing ceasefire mediation hopes against new Houthi threats on Saudi Red Sea oil routes and the ongoing Hormuz tanker attacks.
key_facts: Up from ~$68 before conflict escalation in July
Ceasefire mediation hopes vs new Red Sea threats

headline: Gold steadies near $4,030/oz near 9-month low despite Iran conflict and macro uncertainty
summary: Gold hovered around $4,030 per ounce on Tuesday, close to its lowest level in nine months despite elevated geopolitical uncertainty from the US-Iran conflict. Investors weighed the implications of elevated oil prices for inflation, the Fed's July 28-29 meeting, and the ECB's July 24 decision. The muted gold response suggests markets are not fully pricing a stagflationary scenario.
key_facts: US-Iran conflict and oil inflation pressures key drivers
Fed Jul 28-29 and ECB Jul 24 key risk events

headline: Bitcoin hits two-week high near $65,500 as chip trade turns bullish tailwind
summary: Bitcoin rose to a two-week high near $65,500 on Tuesday as improving sentiment around AI chip stocks boosted broader risk appetite. BTC was up approximately 1% with the global crypto market cap at $2.31 trillion and 24-hour trading volume of $68.99 billion. Lido and Uniswap also rallied alongside BTC and ETH.
key_facts: Chip rally improved risk appetite for crypto

headline: Ethereum gains 1.98% to $1,907 as crypto rallies alongside BTC two-week high
summary: Ethereum rose 1.98% to $1,907.03 on Tuesday alongside Bitcoin's push to a two-week high near $65,500. The broader crypto market added 1.7% on improved chip-sector sentiment and risk-on flows. Lido and Uniswap also rallied.

headline: Alphabet Q2 2026 preview: EPS est. $2.89, revenue $116.84B; $190B AI capex under scrutiny; reports July 22
summary: Alphabet (GOOGL) reports Q2 2026 results after market close on July 22. Consensus calls for EPS of $2.89 on revenue of $116.84B driven by Search and Google Cloud (~63% cloud growth expected). Investors will focus on Alphabet's $190B 2026 capex commitment for AI infrastructure and its impact on free cash flow, which fell from 21% to 9.2% in Q1. GOOGL shares rebounded above $350.
key_facts: FCF margin fell from 21% to 9.2% in Q1

headline: Tesla Q2 2026 preview: record 480,126 deliveries; consensus EPS $0.54, revenue $25.7B; reports July 22
summary: Tesla (TSLA) reports Q2 2026 results after market close on July 22 with a Q&A webcast at 5:30pm ET. Q2 deliveries hit a record 480,126 units (+25% YoY). Consensus EPS is $0.54 (+25% YoY) on revenue of $25.7B (+12% YoY). Investor focus will be on automotive gross margins, FSD autonomous driving progress, and AI and energy storage investment plans.
key_facts: Focus on FSD autonomous driving and AI spend

headline: Big Tech earnings week: 73 reports July 21; GOOGL, TSLA, INTC report July 22
summary: The week of July 21-24 is a pivotal earnings period with 73 companies reporting on Tuesday alone including GM, Halliburton, and 3M before the open. Alphabet, Tesla, and Intel report after close on July 22, with investors scrutinizing AI capital expenditure plans and their translation into revenue and profitability. The week culminates with ECB and Fed decisions.
key_facts: GM, HAL, MMM before open Jul 21
GOOGL, TSLA, INTC after close Jul 22
AI capex and ROI in focus
ECB Jul 24 and Fed Jul 28-29 also this week

headline: ECB July 24 meeting: 95% market probability of hold at 2.25% but oil inflation complicates outlook
summary: The European Central Bank is widely expected to hold its key rate at 2.25% at its July 24 meeting, with prediction markets pricing a 95.3% probability of no change following June's 25bp hike (its first since 2023). Ongoing US-Iran strikes and Hormuz disruptions have introduced inflation uncertainty, with hawks potentially arguing for another 25bp move if energy prices re-accelerate.

headline: Fed expected to hold at 3.63% at July 28-29 FOMC; futures see path rising to 4% by year-end
summary: The Federal Reserve is expected to leave the federal funds rate at 3.63% at its July 28-29 FOMC meeting while preserving the option to tighten further. Futures markets price the rate rising to ~3.8% by October 2026 and approaching 4% by year-end as persistent inflation concerns intensify with the Iran-Hormuz energy shock. The Fed's July 2026 Monetary Policy Report was published July 10.
key_facts: Hormuz energy shock complicates inflation outlook

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield at 4.59% as inflation premium persists from Iran energy shock
summary: The 10-year US Treasury yield was at 4.59% on July 21, elevated by persistent inflation expectations linked to the Iran-Hormuz energy shock and anticipation of the Federal Reserve's July 28-29 FOMC meeting. Futures see rates rising toward 4% by year-end. The 2-year yield was near 4.14% in early July data, keeping the yield curve modestly inverted.
key_facts: Fed expected to hold at 3.63% July 28-29
Hormuz energy shock elevating inflation premium

headline: DXY at 100.92, nearly flat as dollar holds firm on high yields and geopolitical risk
summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY) edged slightly lower to 100.92 (-0.03%) on Tuesday as the dollar remained near recent highs, supported by elevated Treasury yields and lingering geopolitical risks from the Iran-Hormuz conflict. The Japanese yen stayed under pressure with the Bank of Japan maintaining its accommodative stance. UBS projects USD/JPY near 165 and EUR/USD at 1.12 for Q3 2026.
key_facts: Dollar supported by elevated Treasury yields and Iran risk
Yen under pressure from BOJ accommodation

headline: Japanese yen remains under pressure as BOJ keeps accommodative stance; USD/JPY near 165
summary: The Japanese yen remained weak against the US dollar on July 21 as the Bank of Japan maintained its accommodative monetary policy, contrasting with elevated US Treasury yields at 4.59%. UBS projected USD/JPY near 165 for Q3 2026. EUR/USD was capped below 1.12 as geopolitical risk premiums supported the dollar.

headline: First Hawaiian to acquire TriCo Bancshares for $1.77B in all-stock deal, creating $34B Western US bank
summary: First Hawaiian (FHB) agreed on July 13 to acquire TriCo Bancshares (TCBK), parent of Tri Counties Bank, in an all-stock deal valued at ~$1.77B. TriCo shareholders receive 2.095 FHB shares per TCBK share ($63.12/share, a 17.67% premium). The combined entity will hold ~$34 billion in assets, ranking as the 6th-largest bank headquartered in the Western US. Deal expected to close by end of 2026.

headline: Novartis acquires UK's Myricx Bio for up to $1.5B to expand next-generation ADC oncology pipeline
summary: Novartis agreed to acquire Myricx Bio, a UK biotech (Imperial College London spinout), for $1.1 billion upfront plus up to $400 million in milestone payments. Myricx develops antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) using novel N-myristoyltransferase inhibitor (NMTi) payloads targeting B7-H3 and HER2, differentiating from conventional TOPO-1 ADC approaches. Transaction expected to close H2 2026.
key_facts: $1.1B upfront + up to $400M milestones = up to $1.5B
Novel NMTi-based ADC payloads (B7-H3 and HER2 targets)
Distinct from conventional TOPO-1/microtubule ADC payloads

headline: KKR joins US consortium in $7.7B AUD (~$5.3B USD) bid for Australian insurer Steadfast Group
summary: KKR joined Amwins Group and Dragoneer Investment Group in a non-binding bid to acquire Australian insurance broker Steadfast Group (ASX: SDF) for A$6/share, valuing the company at A$7.7 billion (~$5.3B USD). Under the proposed structure, KKR and Dragoneer would assume Steadfast's retail brokerage business, while Amwins would acquire the underwriting agency arm. Steadfast's board noted no certainty of a binding deal.
key_facts: Bid price A$6/share = A$7.7B total (~$5.3B USD)
KKR/Dragoneer take retail brokerage; Amwins takes underwriting agency
Non-binding proposal; no guarantee of binding deal
Steadfast: Australia's largest insurance broker network (500+ brokers)

headline: Citigroup maintains Neutral on Phillips 66, raises price target from $183 to $204
summary: Citigroup maintained its Neutral rating on Phillips 66 (PSX) while raising its price target from $183 to $204. The PT increase likely reflects revised refining margin and oil price assumptions following the Iran-Hormuz escalation and WTI prices moving back into the $80s.

headline: Citigroup maintains Neutral on Starbucks, raises price target from $101 to $108
summary: Citigroup maintained its Neutral rating on Starbucks (SBUX) while raising its price target from $101 to $108. The update reflects stabilization in Starbucks' same-store sales trends and improved operational visibility, though the analyst remains cautious given consumer spending headwinds and elevated costs.
key_facts: Reflects SSS stabilization and improved operational outlook

headline: Rystad Energy warns of significant oil price rebound risk from dual Hormuz-Red Sea supply threat
summary: Rystad Energy warned of the risk of a significant oil price rebound if the Strait of Hormuz conflict combines with the new Houthi embargo on Saudi Red Sea shipments. WTI was trading near $82/bbl on July 21, up from ~$68 before the Iran conflict resumed. With Saudi Arabia now rerouting ~7M bbl/day through the Red Sea bypass, any disruption to that route would close the primary alternative to Hormuz.
key_facts: Rystad: significant rebound risk from dual-route threat
Saudi rerouting ~7M bbl/day through Red Sea bypass
Dual Hormuz+Red Sea blockade scenario unprecedented

headline: Europe faces soft open July 21 as ECB uncertainty and energy costs weigh on margins
summary: European equities faced a softer open on July 21 as traders balanced a heavy corporate earnings calendar, the upcoming ECB July 24 rate decision, and ongoing Hormuz/Red Sea energy cost uncertainty. While Asian markets staged a strong chip-led rebound, Europe remains more exposed to slower-moving margin, energy price, and policy headwinds. EUR/USD stayed capped below 1.12.
key_facts: Europe softer open vs Asia rebound
Heavy corporate earnings week in Europe
ECB July 24 rate decision key risk event
Hormuz and Red Sea energy costs pressure European margins
